title: 'Clarinet Gumbo', Easy on the Ear and Mickey Goldstein's plans
summary: Willard has the RCA album titled 'Clarinet Gumbo', the French title being 'Easy on the Ear'; Bigard is not under contract, and manager Mickey Goldstein wants Duke-style numbers.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: No. It just came in the mail, like I got it last night and I didn't have a chance to play it.
Oh. Where did you get it from?
RCA. They send me certain jazz releases.
Oh, you got it last night?
Uh-huh. But the name of the album is Clarinet Gumbo, not Easy on the Ear.
Oh, yeah?
Barney Bigard and his orchestra, Clarinet Gumbo.
I didn't know that. Maybe that's what they're going to put it out here on.
I guess.
And it was Easy on the Ear --
That's the title in France, huh?
Yeah.
And 'Clarinet Gumbo' was one of the numbers on that?
Yeah.
Well, --
They sent you the whole album?
Uh-huh. There's a picture of you on the cover.
Huh?
That's a nice picture of you on the cover. I didn't even have a chance -- I got in late -- I didn't have a chance to look on the back side to see what all was on it, but -- so I can't --
You see, the reason -- I don't know. They was waiting for the guy, the liner, a new liner, because it's all in French more than over there. *
So they've got a different liner in --
Yeah. Gee, I got to see that.
I thought you would have one.
No, I got the first one in France.
Are you under contract to RCA?
* English language liner notes for Clarinet Gumbo by Frank Driggs.
No. No, I ain't under contract. Mickey Goldsten, you know, --
Uh-huh.
-- he wants me to write some numbers close to something like Duke would have written to --
That should be easy for you.
Huh?
That should be easy for you.
Yeah, and to record it, you know, and have some kind of title about Duke or something.
You're going to do that?
Right after I feel good and I ain't thinking about writing nothing now.

Oh, in that album I got what I call "Satchmo's Dream." In that album you got. But it took them a long time to get that thing out. They keep fooling around. I had to get after Mickey myself, see, because he's the one that sold it to -- did business with RCA.
How long ago did he sell it?

Oh, gosh, it's almost another year. And and I know it's they keep fooling around -- I mean -- (unintelligible) coming out because in France I got in contact with them, you know. I said, "What's cooking here?" So I don't know. Let's cool it for a minute, huh? [PAUSE]
